svg.title: Speed after the top of a climb and the bottom of a descent
svg.desc: Speed as a share of the flat speed that follows, averaged over eight seeds with variability at zero for a recreational runner at an average of 5:30/km, from 60 seconds before to 180 seconds after the top of a 1 km climb at +8 % and the bottom of a 1 km descent at −8 %. On the climb the runner holds about 79 % of the later flat speed. After the crest speed comes back gradually rather than at once: 85 % at 10 s, 92 % at 30 s, 97 % at 60 s, 99 % at 90 s and 100 % at 120 s, staying within 2 % from 73 s. On the descent the runner goes about 115 % of the later flat speed, still 113.5 % at the bottom, and is within 2 % of it from 26 s.
